title: Understanding Logistic Regression
text: In logistic regression, the probability of the binary outcome is modeled using the logistic function, which is denoted as σ. This function maps any real-valued number into the $$(0,1)$$ interval, making it suitable for probability estimation.

title: Comparing Logistic Functions
text: Consider the properties of the logistic function σ. How does the function behave when the input to the function is doubled?

title: Behavior of the Logistic Function
text: The logistic function σ(x) is defined as $$\frac{1}{1+e^{\left(-x\right)}}$$. As $$x$$ increases, σ(x) approaches $$1$$, and as $$x$$ decreases, σ(x) approaches $$0$$.

title: Analyzing the Inequality
text: Given the inequality $$\operatorname{\sigma}\left(X^T \beta\right) \leq \operatorname{\sigma}\left(X^T 2\beta\right)$$, consider the behavior of the logistic function when the input is doubled. Is the inequality always true, sometimes true, or never true?
